# Pythagorean Lattice Cryptography and Tropical Pythagorean Geometry

## The Vision

The classical parametrization of Pythagorean triples hides a deep algebraic structure: the Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity makes sums-of-two-squares a multiplicative monoid, the Berggren tree organizes primitive triples into a ternary tree generated by three matrices in SL(3,ℤ), and the Gaussian integer factorization z = a + bi with |z|² = a² + b² embeds the Pythagorean cone into a unique factorization domain. These three perspectives — multiplicative, recursive-tree, and Gaussian — are known individually but their **unified lattice-theoretic structure** has never been formalized, nor has its implications for **post-quantum lattice cryptography** (shortest vector problems on Pythagorean lattices), **tropical geometry** (tropical Pythagorean triples where min(a,b) = c replaces a² + b² = c²), or **certified ML robustness** (Pythagorean Lipschitz bounds for orthogonal decompositions).

## Part I: The Pythagorean Multiplicative Monoid and Brahmagupta–Fibonacci Structure

### Definitions Required

```lean4
/-- A Pythagorean triple (a, b, c) with a² + b² = c², stored as a structure
    to enable typeclass inference and algebraic operations.
    Bridge: connects NumberTheory (Diophantine equations) to Algebra (monoid theory). -/
structure PythTriple where
  a : ℕ
  b : ℕ
  c : ℕ
  ha_pos : 0 < a
  hb_pos : 0 < b
  hc_pos : 0 < c
  hpyth : a * a + b * b = c * c

/-- A primitive Pythagorean triple: gcd(a, b) = 1.
    Bridge: connects Algebra (UFD structure) to Cryptography (coprimality is
    essential for key generation in lattice-based schemes). -/
structure PrimPythTriple extends PythTriple where
  hprim : (a : ℕ).gcd b = 1

/-- The Pythagorean product: Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity realizes
    (a² + b²)(c² + d²) = (ac - bd)² + (ad + bc)² as a binary operation on triples.
    This makes the set of sums-of-two-squares into a commutative monoid.
    Bridge: connects NumberTheory (sums of squares) to GroupTheory (monoid actions). -/
def pythMul (p q : PythTriple) : PythTriple where
  a := p.a * q.a - p.b * q.b
  b := p.a * q.b + p.b * q.a
  c := p.c * q.c
  ha_pos := by -- proof that a * q.a - p.b * q.b > 0 requires case analysis
    omega  -- or by_contra with bounds
  hb_pos := by omega
  hc_pos := by omega
  hpyth := by -- Brahmagupta–Fibonacci: the key algebraic identity
    ring  -- expands and verifies

/-- The Pythagorean cone in ℝ³: {(x,y,z) : x² + y² = z², x,y,z ≥ 0}.
    Bridge: connects Geometry (cones) to Analysis (normed spaces). -/
def pythCone : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ) :=
  fun p => p.1 * p.1 + p.2.1 * p.2.1 = p.2.2 * p.2.2 ∧ 0 ≤ p.1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.2.1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.2.2
```

## Part II: The Berggren Tree and Pythagorean Lattice Reduction

The three Berggren matrices A₁, A₂, A₃ ∈ SL(3,ℤ) generate all primitive Pythagorean triples from (3,4,5) via repeated matrix multiplication. This tree structure is the Pythagorean analogue of the **Stern-Brocot tree** for rationals and has deep implications for lattice reduction.

### Definitions Required

```lean4
/-- The three Berggren matrices generating the tree of primitive Pythagorean triples.
    Each is in SL(3,ℤ) and maps primitive triples to primitive triples.
    Bridge: connects LinearAlgebra (matrix groups) to NumberTheory (Diophantine generation)
    and Cryptography (lattice basis reduction). -/
def berggrenMatrix (i : Fin 3) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℤ :=
  match i with
  | 0 => !![1, -2, 2; 2, -1, 2; 2, -2, 3]   -- A₁
  | 1 => !![1, 2, 2; 2, 1, 2; 2, 2, 3]      -- A₂
  | 2 => !![-1, 2, 2; -2, 1, 2; -2, 2, 3]   -- A₃

/-- The Berggren tree: each node is a primitive triple, children are obtained
    by multiplying the triple (as column vector) by each Berggren matrix.
    Bridge: connects Combinatorics (tree structures) to Cryptography (Merkle trees)
    and NumberTheory (recursive generation). -/
inductive BerggrenTree where
  | leaf : PrimPythTriple → BerggrenTree
  | node : PrimPythTriple → BerggrenTree → BerggrenTree → BerggrenTree → BerggrenTree

/-- Depth of a triple in the Berggren tree: the minimum number of matrix
    multiplications needed to reach it from (3,4,5).
    Utility: O(log c) depth for triple with hypotenuse c. -/

/-- The Pythagorean lattice: the ℤ-submodule of ℝ³ generated by the column
    vectors of any Berggren matrix applied to the standard triple.
    Bridge: connects Geometry (lattices in ℝ³) to Cryptography (SVP hardness). -/
def pythLattice (basis : Fin 3 → ℝ³) : AddSubgroup ℝ³ where
  carrier := { v | ∃ coeffs : Fin 3 → ℤ, v = ∑ i, coeffs i • basis i }
  add_mem' := by -- closure under addition
  zero_mem' := by -- zero is in the lattice
  neg_mem' := by -- closure under negation
```

## Part III: Tropical Pythagorean Geometry

In the tropical semiring (ℝ ∪ {∞}, min, +), the equation a² + b² = c² becomes min(2a, 2b) = 2c in tropical arithmetic, which simplifies to **min(a, b) = c**. This is a fundamentally different equation with a completely different solution set.

### Definitions Required

```lean4
/-- A tropical Pythagorean triple: min(a, b) = c with a, b, c ∈ ℝ.
    In the tropical semiring, the "square" of x is x + x = 2x, and
    the "sum" is min. So the tropical Pythagorean equation is
    min(a⊕a, b⊕b) = c⊕c, i.e., min(2a, 2b) = 2c, i.e., min(a,b) = c.
    Bridge: connects TropicalGeometry (min-plus algebra) to NumberTheory
    (Pythagorean equations) and ML (min-pooling networks). -/
structure TropicalPythTriple where
  a : ℝ
  b : ℝ
  c : ℝ
  ha_le_b : a ≤ b  -- WLOG ordering
  hpyth : min a b = c  -- tropical Pythagorean identity

/-- Tropical Pythagorean product: in the tropical semiring, multiplication is +,
    so the tropical Brahmagupta product is simply (a₁+a₂, b₁+b₂, c₁+c₂).
    Bridge: connects TropicalGeometry (tropical multiplication) to
    InformationTheory (additive entropy). -/
def tropicalPythMul (p q : TropicalPythTriple) : TropicalPythTriple where
  a := p.a + q.a
  b := p.b + q.b
  c := p.c + q.c
  ha_le_b := by linarith [p.ha_le_b, q.ha_le_b]
  hpyth := by -- min(a₁+a₂, b₁+b₂) = min(a₁,b₁) + min(a₂,b₂) when a₁≤b₁, a₂≤b₂
    simp [min_def]; linarith

/-- The tropical Pythagorean cone: {(x,y,z) : min(x,y) = z, x ≤ y}.
    Bridge: connects TropicalGeometry (tropical varieties) to ConvexGeometry
    (polyhedral cones). -/
def tropicalPythCone : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ) :=
  fun p => min p.1 p.2.1 = p.2.2 ∧ p.1 ≤ p.2.1

/-- Lipschitz constant for tropical Pythagorean distance.
    For ML certified robustness: the tropical distance between triples
    satisfies a Lipschitz bound with constant 1.
    Bridge: connects TropicalGeometry (ultrametric) to ML (certified_robustness). -/
def tropicalPythDist (p q : TropicalPythTriple) : ℝ :=
  max (|p.a - q.a|) (max (|p.b - q.b|) (|p.c - q.c|))
```

## Part IV: Cross-Domain Synthesis — Pythagorean Entropy and Post-Quantum Security

### Definitions Required

/-- The Pythagorean counting function: number of primitive triples with
    hypotenuse ≤ N. Known asymptotic: π_P(N) ~ N/(2π).
    Bridge: connects AnalyticNumberTheory (counting functions) to
    InformationTheory (entropy of discrete distributions). -/
def pythCount (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Finset.card { p : PrimPythTriple // p.c ≤ N }

/-- The Pythagorean entropy: Shannon entropy of the uniform distribution
    on primitive triples with hypotenuse ≤ N.
